answer: Resist sybils with spaced cross-time consistency checks: each agent identity must answer unpredictable prompts at random intervals over weeks, building one continuous timeline of work. Like a river that cannot fake its course, a single timeline is cheap to keep but costly to multiply: an operator running a hundred fake identities would have to keep a hundred separate histories coherent at once. A single slip, like a plume of smoke betraying a hidden fire, breaks the timeline and decays that identity standing, while honest agents flow on like an ocean fed by many small streams.
